activation.reactionTrigger: When you have the high ground

system.description:
You suddenly decelerate, causing your foe to fly past you and into your gunsights.

Choose another starfighter operating in the same combat zone which has locked on to you. The starfighter makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, you make an attack against the target.

Choose one creature within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you and has a clear path to you. Make a Persuasion check against the creature’s passive Insight. On a success, you and the creature are fixated on each other until the end of your next turn, and it must spend its next turn safely moving as close to you as possible.

While fixated in this way, you have disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than the creature, and the creature has disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than you.

You draw up the dead to do your horrible bidding. Choose a number of squares equal to your Charisma modifier within 30 feet. These squares become occupied with shadowy apparitions, which have an AC equal to 10 + your Charisma modifier your Maneuver DC and 10 hit points. Each apparition has its own reaction for the purpose of making opportunity attacks, which it makes using your attack bonus, but cannot help flank. On a hit, the creature takes damage equal to your Charisma modifier and you gain hit points equal to the damage dealt. You can also use your own reaction to direct an apparition to make another opportunity attack if it has already used its own.

While maintaining this stance, you can forgo your movement to instead move any apparition the same number of squares. This can be split among multiple apparitions, as long as you have the movement available. The apparitions must stay within 30 feet of you or they vanish. This stance ends early if all apparitions are destroyed.

The hunter must be focused and swift to bring down their prey.

When you enter this stance, choose a creature you can see. You gain an expertise die on on attack rolls made against the chosen creature and make all attack rolls against other creatures with disadvantage. Your Speed increases by 10 feet when moving closer to the chosen creature, so long as you can see it, but your passive Perception against other creatures is reduced by 3. While in this stance, you can use a bonus action to choose a different creature to target.

You imbue your strike with additional psychic energy.

When you next hit a target with a starglaive before the start of your next turn, you deal an additional 2d6 psychic damage.

The icon of decorum, your presence leaves no doubt of your whereabouts. When you have the attention you seek, you can add extra flourish that makes hearts swoon.

Allies within 30 feet of you are always aware of your location, regardless of effects or cover that would obfuscate you. You can target them and they can target you as if you can see or hear each other.

Additionally, you are always aware of the location of any creature fixated on you, and you can target them as if you can see or hear them.

Finally, if you willingly end this stance on your turn, any creature fixated on you is also rattled for as long as they are fixated in that way.

You and your wingmen corral your targets to keep them from escaping.

Whenever you successfully lock on to a starfighter, any other ships in the formation can use their reaction to lock on to that same target. While locked on ships in the formation have advantage on attacks against it. If you lose the lock on a target other ships in the formation lose that lock as well.

You instinctively identify and leverage the perfect angles and impact points for throwing your weapon.

Make a ranged weapon attack, as well as any additional attacks granted by Extra Attack. Until the start of your next turn, when you make a ranged weapon attack with a weapon that has the thrown property, its ranges are doubled, you gain an expertise die on the attack and damage rolls, and on a hit that does not deal piercing damage the weapon rebounds, returning to your hand at the end of the attack. If a weapon returns, you can immediately use your reaction to spend 1 exertion point and make a melee weapon attack against a target within reach.

Abilities: Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom

You precisely strike at your opponent’s knees or other load-bearing point. The target makes a Constitution saving throw against your maneuver DC. On a failure, it takes your basic melee damage and its base walking speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

You break direct line of sight with your enemies by flying into an area that’s dangerous or obscured.

You may only perform this starship maneuver while operating in a combat zone with the obscuring property. Any ships with a lock on you must make a Wisdom saving throw or lose their lock.

Abilities: Intelligence, Wisdom

You attempt to catch your opponent off guard by stomping on its toes or or striking at some other vulnerable part of its anatomy. The target makes a Constitution saving throw against your maneuver DC. On a failure, the creature takes your basic melee damage damage and is slowed until the end of its next turn. At the Narrator’s discretion, this dueling maneuver may not be effective against certain creatures, or you may have to succeed at a relevant knowledge check to be aware of a creature’s weak points.

With a little quick thinking on your feet, you can adjust your attack strategy to find additional ways to hit an opponent.

When you activate this maneuver, you take the Attack action and make a weapon attack, as well as any additional attacks granted by Extra Attack. Immediately after, you can make two unarmed strikes against the target of your last attack.

You’ve waited until just the right moment to spring your ambush and bring down your quarry.

When you activate this maneuver, choose a creature you are currently hidden from and take the Attack action and make a weapon attack, as well as any additional attacks granted by Extra Attack. Any attacks you make in this way are made with advantage (instead of only the first as normal for surprised creatures) and each deals one additional weapon damage die.

Despite any number of intrusions into your mind or distractions surrounding you, your mind is unimpeded and on task.

When an effect causes you to be charmed or confused, you can use your reaction to prevent it.

With utter certainty, you announce your impending success and the impressive means by which you’ll achieve it. The sheer audacity of the attempt makes it that much more inspiring if you succeed.

When you take the Attack or Tumble actions or use a Basic Maneuver, but before any dice are rolled, you can use your reaction to activate this maneuver. When using this maneuver, you can’t gain the benefits of any expertise die for attack rolls, ability checks, or saving throws made during the triggering action.

If you succeed, all allies (other than you) within 30 feet that were able to see you do so gain advantage on their next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw if it is made within a number of rounds equal to your Charisma modifier. If the roll for the triggering action is a critical success, this duration becomes 1 minute.

Attentive and watchful, you snap off a shot at whatever dared to try and catch you by surprise.

When you are surprised, you may immediately draw a ranged or thrown weapon and make a single ranged weapon attack at the start of initiative.

You deactivate your blade momentarily just before it would be blocked by your enemy’s, and reactivate it to finish the strike.

When you make an attack against an enemy with a starglaive or an energy-imbued weapon, you make the attack at advantage using a maneuver to neatly bypass their defence.

You put your game face on as you strap into the pilot’s seat.

While piloting a vehicle:

  • You gain an expertise die on ability checks made to drive or pilot a vehicle.
  • You can take the Accelerate vehicle action as a reaction.
  • Attacks against you, the vehicle, and its cargo and passengers have disadvantage unless the vehicle is Titanic.
  • If a collision occurs, after determining the collision damage roll the vehicle’s collision damage a second time. You can reduce the damage your vehicle sustains by the result of the second roll. If you reduce the damage to 0 the collision is avoided altogether.

Physical comedy resonates best if performed in tandem, and with the right footwork even the unsuspecting can be made into an impromptu stage partner.

When you fall prone you can use your reaction to make a Knockdown basic maneuver against an adjacent creature, forcing it to make a Dexterity saving throw or fall prone with you.

Even the swiftest and most erratic quarries have predictable patterns in their movements for the hawk-eyed hunter.

Until the beginning of your next turn, any creature that you target with a ranged weapon attack does not add its Dexterity modifier to its Armor Class for the purposes of these attacks.

Focusing your psychic energy, you strike an object with concentrated force.

You make a single attack against an unattended object of size Large or smaller, such as a door, with a starglaive maul. On a hit, the object gains the broken condition. If the object is reinforced, you must instead beat its AC by 4 points or more in order to sunder it.

You can uplift an ally’s spirits and boost their endurance.

Select a friendly target that can see, hear, feel, or otherwise sense your presence. You impart the target with temporary hit points equal to 1d6 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier (minimum 0).

Suddenly the empty space in front of you is occupied and you desperately try to pull your ship out of a collision course!

When you fail a saving throw to avoid a collision or attempted ramming, use your reaction to reroll the failed saving throw, taking the new result.

You use irregularities in the space-time continuum to continuously jink your ship, making it impossible to target you. Until the start of your next turn, when an attack would hit your starfighter, it misses instead, and when you would fail a saving throw, you succeed instead.

When your opponent disarms you, you recall your weapon instantly.

If you are disarmed, you can use your reaction to instantly teleport your starglaive back to your hand.

With a gesture, you telekinetically pull a distant foe towards you and strike them with your starglaive.

One target you can see or sense within 30 feet makes a Strength saving throw or is pulled towards you until it hits a stationary barrier (e.g. a wall or force field) or is within reach of your melee attacks. If the target ends up within reach of your melee attacks, you immediately take the Attack action and make a weapon attack, as well as any additional attacks granted by Extra Attack.

Abilities: Strength, Dexterity

You drive your enemy where you want it to go. When you activate this dueling maneuver, you take the Attack action and make a weapon attack, as well as any additional attacks granted by Extra Attack. Until the start of your next turn, when you hit the target with a weapon attack, you can move it to an adjacent square of your choice (maximum 3 times). This movement does not provoke an opportunity attack.

You catch yourself about to blunder, steady yourself, and adjust your aim.

When you make an attack roll but before you know the result of your attack, you can use your reaction to reroll that attack, taking the new result.

With your quarry in sight, you make a final sprint to close the distance and strike like a predator pouncing on its prey.

Move up to your Speed in a straight line. If at the end of your movement there is a creature within your reach, you can take the Attack action with a melee weapon, as well as any additional attacks granted by Extra Attack. The first attack you make as part of this maneuver has advantage.

You position yourselves to put active eyes on as much of the area as possible.

Starfighter pilots in this formation gain an expertise die on Perception checks and when rolling for initiative.

With a swift, clean blow you sever the limb of your opponent.

Make an attack against a creature within reach with a starglaive blade or polearm. This attack bypasses the target’s resistance to damage, but its immunity to damage is unchanged. Your attack is made at disadvantage. On a hit you cleanly sever one of the target’s limbs and the target takes an additional 1d10 psychic damage. In addition, the creature suffers a level of strife. The limb is not severed if the target has immunity to the weapon’s damage or the creature is two or more sizes larger than you.

The end of many a good pilot has been a turret or enemy starfighter that stayed locked on for just a bit too long. It’s best to shake them off with some evasive flying.

One ship of your choice that is locked on to you makes a Dexterity saving throw or loses its lock on you.

You stand firm, deflecting incoming missile attacks.

While you are wielding a starglaive, you can use your reaction to slice through or block ammunition when you are hit by a ranged weapon attack. When you do so, your AC against ranged attacks is increased by double your Wisdom modifier (including against the triggering attack) until the end of your next turn.

No obstacle can impede you, and no noise can distract you—there is only you, your quarry, and your determination to bring it down.

When you activate this maneuver, choose a creature you can see. Until the start of your next turn, weapon attacks you make against the chosen creature ignore any condition, effect, or circumstance that would impose disadvantage.
You gain an expertise die on Persuasion checks made in combat.

With one true strike, you are able to rapidly repeat the same movements and land the rest of your strikes on the same exact spot.

When you successfully hit a creature with a ranged weapon attack, you can use your reaction to zero in on the target. Until the beginning of your next turn, if you make additional weapon attacks against the same creature you gain an expertise die on the attack, and on a hit your attack becomes a critical hit. If your attack would already have been a critical hit, the target takes additional damage equal to twice your proficiency bonus and is knocked prone.

Confident in your ability to prevail, you handicap yourself, granting your opponent a chance at victory and renewing your resolve.

Choose one creature within your reach. The creature gains an expertise die on attacks against you until the end of your next turn. For this duration, you gain advantage on saving throws against being frightened, fixated, charmed, or rattled. Additionally, if you are currently affected by any of these conditions, you can immediately roll a save against one of them, potentially ending the effect early.

Amidst the chaos of combat, you set your attention on your quarry while keeping yourself hidden from them.

While in combat, choose a creature you can see. You take the Hide action, rolling your Stealth check with advantage. The chosen creature’s passive Perception is considered to be reduced by 5 for the purposes of detecting you, while other creatures consider theirs to be reduced by 3. As long as you remain hidden and do not move more than half your Speed in a round, any creatures trying to actively detect you make their Perception checks with disadvantage.

While aboard a capital ship, you can recognize patterns and strategies, then intuit and perform actions that could dynamically tilt the battle in your favor.

When you activate this maneuver, you can immediately make a system action using the deck you are crewing. Any attack rolls made with that system action gain advantage and any saving throws made against it have disadvantage. In addition, until the start of your next turn both you and any allies you communicate with each gain an expertise die for one saving throw, ability check, or attack made before the start of your next turn.

You mask each other’s energy signatures and try to fly under the radar.

Starfighter pilots in this formation gain an expertise die on Stealth checks.

You ignore distractions and focus on the task at hand.

You make all saving throws to resist the frightened and rattled conditions at advantage.

When you activate this maneuver, you take the Tumble action. You may make a Charisma saving throw instead of a Dexterity saving throw against the target’s combat maneuver DC. If you have proficiency with Performance, you gain an expertise die on the save. This expertise die increases to 1d6 if you have a specialization in acting or dancing. Only one speciality can apply to this roll. On a success, the creature can’t take opportunity attacks against you until the beginning of your next turn.

By first aligning with then clashing violently against the exact rhythm of your opponent’s movements, breath, and even heartbeat, your physical touch interrupts their life force.

A living creature you touch makes a Dexterity saving throw or takes psychic damage equal to 6d8 + your Wisdom modifier and is stunned until the end of your next turn. On a success the creature takes half the damage and is slowed until the end of your next turn instead of stunned. A creature immune to being stunned automatically succeeds on its saving throw. The effort of activating this maneuver drains you and you are rattled until the end of your next turn.

When you realize an expedient exit is needed (perhaps due to the arrival of enemy reinforcements), you can quickly identify the best route and create the space for you and your allies to make a hasty escape.

You use your reaction to make a Wisdom (Deception) check opposed by an enemy’s passive Perception. On a success, you and allies within 30 feet (or within the same region during a space battle) can take the Disengage action and move up to twice your Speed (or engage your FTL engines) without invoking an opportunity attack.

activation.reactionTrigger: When you realize an expedient exit is needed (perhaps due to the arrival of enemy reinforcements)

system.description:
Lining up the shots, you carefully pick out your target along a ship’s massive frame.

Choose a deck or weapon system on a capital ship in your combat zone and make an attack targeting that ship. These attacks have disadvantage if the chosen deck is a bridge or engines deck. Every time you hit with an attack made this way, the target ship makes a Constitution saving throw with a –2 penalty for every 10 damage dealt by the attack. On a failed save a deck suffers the deck damaged critical malfunction, or a weapon system suffers the weapon system damaged critical malfunction. A deck that already has the deck damage critical malfunction suffers the deck disabled critical malfunction instead.

Abilities: Charisma

You taunt your opponent into attacking out of rage instead of skill. When you are the targeted by a weapon attack, you can use your reaction to taunt your opponent. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw against your maneuver DC. On a failure, it makes the attack at disadvantage, but deals an additional damage die if the attack is successful.

You have a level of awareness and the presence of mind to support an ally in need.

You take the Help action.

You see through all distractions and obstacles to strike true.

When you activate this maneuver, you take the Attack action and make a ranged weapon attack, as well as any additional attacks granted by Extra Attack. Until the start of your next turn, your ranged attack rolls ignore half cover and treat three-quarters cover as half cover instead.

You beckon someone to your side with infectious fervor, be they stranger or comrade-in-arms.

Choose one conscious non-hostile creature within 30 feet of you that can see you. The creature can use its reaction to move up to its Speed in a straight line toward you. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

If the creature enters your reach, you can use your reaction to draw one item and administer it to the creature if it is willing. The item must be a potion, medicine, or some other beneficial consumable.

A duel is not fittingly dramatic without the proper stakes. You lock blades with a worthy foe, and fight to the bitter end. To the winner goes the glory.

Choose one creature within 30 feet that can see or hear you, whose CR is no less than half your level, and has a clear path to you. Make a Persuasion check against the creature’s passive Insight. On a success, you and the creature enter a duel and are fixated on each other until either you or the challenged creature dies, drops to 0 hit points or otherwise becomes incapacitated, or either ends their turn out of line of sight from the other. It also ends if you use this maneuver on a different creature.

At the beginning of each of your turns, you both must move closer to each other if your opponent is not within your reach for a melee weapon attack or attempt to overcome an effect or obstacle that blocks you from doing so. Once within range, you and the creature must make at least one melee weapon attack against each other on your turns. Neither of you can willingly target other creatures and both of you gain a +4 bonus to your AC and saving throws against against attacks or effects made by other creatures.

If one creature drops to 0 hit points during the duel, the other creature gains an expertise die to attack and damage rolls for the rest of the combat.

With a flurry of lightning-fast cuts, you sever all of your opponent’s limbs.

Make an attack against a creature within reach with a starglaive blade or polearm. This attack bypasses the target’s resistance to damage, but its immunity to damage is unchanged. Your attack is made at disadvantage.

On a hit you cleanly sever 1d4 of the target’s limbs and the target takes an additional 1d10 psychic damage per limb severed. In addition, the creature suffers a level of strife for each limb severed. The limb is not severed if the target has immunity to the weapon’s damage or the creature is two or more sizes larger than you.

You fly dangerously close to avoid the guns firing above you and line up a perfect shot, but doing so puts you right in the crosshairs of the close range guns.

You may only perform this starship maneuver while operating in a combat zone surrounding a capital ship. Until the end of your next turn, any attacks that target you have disadvantage, and you have disadvantage on saving throws against weapons with the anti-starfighter property.

Any attacks you make during your next turn have advantage and their critical hit range is increased by 1 (for example a weapon that would score a critical hit on a 20 instead scores a critical hit on an attack roll of 19–20).

Not to be kept down, you return to the battle, defiant and ready for more.

If you are at 0 hit points and regain hit points, such as from a maneuver, effect, or spell, you can use your reaction to immediately stand up from being prone without spending movement.

Additionally, choose up to three creatures that can see you. Each creature gains an expertise die to the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw it makes within 1 minute. You can use this reaction even if you are incapacitated.

Dispensing with targeting systems and electronic aids, you focus your mind and make an attack out of pure instinct. Your next attack with a starfighter weapon before the start of your next turn automatically hits its target.

Relaxing your mind, you trust your instincts, allowing your psionic energy to guide your actions.

When you roll a 9 or less on an attack roll with a starglaive, you may treat that roll as though it were a 10.

Your attacks are ferocious enough that nothing can stop them.

Attacks you make with a starglaive bypass immunity to its damage until the start of your next turn.

A tossed rose, a blown kiss—you acknowledge someone whose eye was caught by your swagger.

Choose one creature within 30 feet that can see you. Make a Performance check against the creature’s passive Insight. On a success, the creature is fixated on you until the start of your next turn.

Prerequisite: Steel Protector

Now when you enshroud yourself with divine metal you can feel the strength of it in your very bones. Whenever you use your Metal Skin feature with a spell slot of 3rd-level or higher, you gain the following additional benefits:

  • Your carrying capacity doubles.
  • Your unarmed strikes deal an extra 1d8 damage (instead of 1d4) and count as magical for the purposes of overcoming damage resistances and immunities.
  • You gain proficiency with the @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-maneuvers.Item.l8e05qfdh3bwce7z]{Hurl Ally} maneuver and do not have to spend exertion to activate it. In addition, you count as one size category larger when using it.

Additionally, when using a spell slot of 4th-level, your Metal Skin lasts for 10 minutes, and when using a 5th-level or higher spell slot your Metal Skin lasts for 1 hour.

The lands of Albia are not for the faint of heart, the very ground quickly shifting between difficult and dangerous. Even established roads are prone to bandits, sudden changes in weather patterns, and warlords trying to make a name for themselves. Albian Hillrunners are couriers between the lordships of central Elissar, trained to survive and thrive in the wilderness while withstanding the forces of nature.

  • Your Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You gain an expertise die on ability checks and saving throws made against terrain.
  • You gain an expertise die on Athletics checks made to Sprint.
  • Once each week while traveling in the wilderness you can find a location that can be used as a temporary haven for a number of days equal to half your proficiency bonus. After you use this feature in a location, that location cannot be made into a temporary haven again.

Prerequisite: Noble background or the favor of a noble

You have befriended or impressed one of Allesund’s nobles, earning you the services of one of their most trusted advisors. Your Wisdom or Charisma score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20. In addition, your Prestige rating increases by 1 and you gain a seasoned courtier.
system.prerequisite: Noble background or the favor of a noble

system.description:
You’ve had your fair share of rough and tumble experiences in back alleys, sewers, and other urban environs.

  • You have advantage on Investigation and Perception checks made to find your way into, navigate through, and detect secrets in sewers.
  • You have advantage on saving throws made against traps and diseases found in alleys, sewers, and other places of urban filth.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Audio Engineer feat

You can leverage technology to amplify your performances. You gain the following benefits:

  • When one of your spell inventions would fizzle out, you may immediately expend a spell slot of the same level or higher as the spell cast by the spell invention to prevent it from fizzling.
  • When you cast a bard or artificer spell using a spell invention, you may add the results of the fizzle die to attack rolls made as part of the casting of the spell for 1 round. Alternatively, creatures and objects that make a saving throw caused by the spell must reduce their saving throw totals by the results of the fizzle die for 1 round.
  • If you reach 10th level in bard, you gain the following benefit: when using a spell invention to cast a bard or artificer spell with a casting time of an action, you can immediately cast a bard or artificer cantrip with a casting time of one action as a bonus action. Once you have used this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

Design Note on Amped Up

When artificers reach 10th level, the size of their fizzle die increases, improving the power of this feat. Bards have therefore been given an additional bonus at the same level to compensate.

You are proficient in the Engineering skill and either smith’s tools or tinker’s tools.

Choose one gadget from the list available to the Gadgeteer fighter. You have a basic codex with instructions to create that gadget. You can also add more gadgets to your codex by learning from other inventors, typically by spending one day of down time with that inventor’s aid and spending 100 gp for the necessary materials to tinker.

Whenever you complete a short or long rest you can prepare one copy of any gadget you know how to make. If you prepare more gadgets, your previous gadgets cease to work. If you are also a fighter with the Gadgeteer archetype, the gadget from this feat stacks with the number you can prepare from your class.

Most gadgets can only be used once, then become inert. If a gadget calls for a saving throw, the DC is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier.

You also can cast a special version of @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.6l4bmc7ovgcn2c9k]{find familiar} as a ritual, requiring 10 gp of arcanotechnological parts, which must be assembled together into a pet contraption.

The contraption uses the same list of beasts as @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.6l4bmc7ovgcn2c9k]{find familiar} , but it is a construct instead of a beast. It is resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons that aren’t adamantine. It is immune to poison and psychic damage, and cannot be charmed , exhausted , frightened , paralyzed , petrified , or poisoned . It has darkvision out to 120 feet and understands your languages, but cannot speak. If the contraption is reduced to 0 hit points, you can repair it by using this ritual again.

You can spend an action to place a gadget into your contraption, or to remove or swap a gadget you had previously integrated. Even if you can make more than one gadget at a time, your contraption can hold at most one. The contraption can then spend the appropriate action, bonus action, or reaction to use the gadget, using your attack bonus or other stats to determine its efficacy.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: 3 levels in artificer , 3 levels in bard

You can craft customized instruments to enhance your performances. You gain the following benefits:

  • Your Intelligence or Charisma score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You may prepare bard spells you know as spell inventions. Doing so does not prevent you from casting such spells using spell slots. You may not prepare or cast a bard spell above your artificer spell level maximum this way. Artificer is your spellcasting class for such spell inventions.
  • Choose a spell from the bard spell list that is of a level you can cast both as a bard and an artificer. It does not need to be one you already know. You may prepare one additional spell invention utilizing the chosen spell. You are not able to cast the spell if you do not otherwise know it or have it prepared. You can choose a different spell each time you take a level in the artificer or bard classes.
  • You may use a spell invention as a spell focus for your bard spells, and you may use art specialties with artificer spells. Whenever you prepare a spell invention, you may choose to create it as a musical instrument with which you are proficient.
system.prerequisite: 3 levels in artificer , 3 levels in bard

system.description:
Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Mental Mastery

Your mental prowess reaches incredible heights and lesser minds are as open to you as a tavern’s door. You can spend 2 exertion points to cast @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.4rgo85d49qwancup]{detect thoughts} without the need for any components. When a creature makes a saving throw against your @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.4rgo85d49qwancup]{detect thoughts}, you can spend another 2 exertion points to give it disadvantage . Finally, you can spend an additional 2 exertion points to also affect a creature under the effects of your @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.4rgo85d49qwancup]{detect thoughts} with a @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.i0o4xqqd86vdkwwu]{zone of truth} spell without the need for any components.

Many people smuggle banned goods, invasive plant life, or dangerous creatures between locations, but you’ve learned some additional tricks. You gain the following benefits:

  • Your Charisma increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • When attempting to hide an object or creature amid cargo you can sacrifice Supply based on the creature or object’s size to gain advantage on Stealth checks to conceal the creature or object: Small or smaller—1 Supply, Medium—4 Supply, Large—16 Supply, Huge—32 Supply.
  • You gain advantage on any skill check involving bribery.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: 3 levels in fighter, 3 levels in herald

Though learning how to harness your divine power was rigorous and involved a great deal of suffering, you have learned to transform some of it into a shining second skin that protects you from harm.

Metal Skin. You can use a bonus action and expend a herald spell slot to cover your body in a bronze alloy of divinity and metal that protects you from harm. For the next minute, whenever you take damage other than lightning or psychic damage, you reduce the damage you take by an amount equal to the level of the expended spell slot (before calculating resistances ). You can end the effect as a free action.
system.prerequisite: 3 levels in fighter, 3 levels in herald

system.description:
You move through a battlefield with inspiring grace. As long as you’re not encumbered or wearing heavy armor, you gain the following benefits.

You have a climb speed equal to your base speed. If you fall intentionally while moving, determine the damage you take as if you’d fallen a distance shortened by 10 feet times your proficiency bonus.

When you have a running start, add your proficiency bonus to the number of feet of your high jump, and five times your proficiency bonus to the number of feet of your long jump distance.

Whenever you Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Hide, one ally who can see you can use a bonus action on their next turn to perform the same action. A creature can only benefit from this feature once between short or long rests.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Psi Trooper feat

Experienced psi troopers can psionically will their weapons into finding their marks, curving bullets, lasers, and blades. Whenever you make a weapon attack you can spend a psionic  point to gain advantage. Any attack you make in this way ignores the benefits of half and three-quarters cover.

You’re used to eking out a living in urban environments, finding ways to scrounge and scavenge everything you need to survive.

  • Raise your Dexterity or Wisdom attribute by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You can perform the Gather Components, Harvest, and Hunt and Gather journey activities while in urban environments.
  • Once per long rest , you can stretch your Supply further than it would normally go by supplementing it with local bounty. You can make a Survival check when preparing a meal (with a difficulty determined by the region’s tier) to halve the Supply required to feed up to four creatures. On a failure, each Supply can only feed a single creature.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: 3 levels in rogue , 3 levels in savant

You specialize in working undercover. You gain the following benefits:

  • Your Dexterity or Intelligence score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You can prepare a savant trick and perform a Cunning Action using the same bonus action.
  • You can use flourish tricks with ranged attacks if they also qualify as sneak attacks.
  • You can make sneak attacks using improvised weapons in addition to finesse and ranged weapons.
system.prerequisite: 3 levels in rogue , 3 levels in savant

system.description:
Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Teleporting Combatant

Not only does your ability to step between reality’s folds become as easy as walking, your control over this unique power becomes so complete that you can place the ground beneath your feet no matter what the surface, enabling you to safely teleport onto walls, ceilings, and the like.

You also gain the Spider Climb feature.

Spider Climb. You gain a climb speed equal to your Speed, and you can climb even on difficult surfaces and upside down on ceilings.

You create a strong sympathetic bond with cybernetics that you have installed. You gain the following benefits.

  • Your Constitution score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You can have an additional enhancement implant that doesn’t count against your proficiency bonus limit.
  • This feat can be taken multiple times, increasing your Constitution score and choosing a different enhancement implant each time.

You are the nightmare of most hackers, and gain the following benefits:

  • Your Charisma or Wisdom increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • When opposing a hacking attempt you increase the speed of the countdown by 1 degree, from slow (removing 6s) to medium (removing 5-6s), to fast (removing 4-6s).
  • During a short or long rest you can reinforce a personal device, including cybernetic implants, causing hacking attempts against it to be made at disadvantage until your next long rest.
  • The roll to hack any system on a capital ship deck that you are crewing is made at disadvantage.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: 3 levels in adept, 3 levels in rogue

Throughout the process of honing your body and mind, your keen senses revealed folds within the very firmament of reality—anomalies that you have learned how to exploit to move between increasingly distant points with just a step. You gain the following special focus feature:

Dimensional Step. Once on your turn, you can use a reaction to spend up to a number of exertion points equal to your proficiency bonus to teleport to an unoccupied space that you can see at a cost of 1 exertion point per 10 feet of distance. Additionally, each time you teleport you can choose to appear in your chosen space lightly obscured by a 5-foot square area of fog, allowing you to immediately take the Hide action. The fog dissipates at the start of your next turn or can be dispersed by a moderate wind (at least 10 miles per hour).
system.prerequisite: 3 levels in adept, 3 levels in rogue

system.description:
You unfortunately have great experience rescuing allies on the battlefield. As a bonus action, you can choose one or two bloodied creatures within 10 feet of you, potentially including yourself. If they are at 0 hit points, your heroic example rouses them to 1 hit point. If they are prone, you move to the nearest open space and lift them to a stand. The creatures can each move their speed without provoking opportunity attacks , and until the end of your next turn, attack rolls against them have disadvantage, and they have advantage on saving throws.

Once you use this feat, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

In addition, you are proficient with water vehicles

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: 3 levels in artificer , 3 levels in cleric

You have discovered the intrinsic link between divinity and artifice. You gain the following benefits:

  • Your Intelligence or Wisdom score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You can create a flask of holy water using Tactical Chemistry
  • Whenever you make an Engineering check using Intelligence, you may add your Wisdom modifier.
  • Spells and effects you cause that specify that they do not affect constructs or undead now affect constructs.
  • When you use Turn Undead, you can choose to also (or only) affect constructs.
  • You can use your tools of artifice as a spellcasting focus for your cleric spells.
system.prerequisite: 3 levels in artificer , 3 levels in cleric

system.description:
In a band every musician has to know their bandmates’ parts in case they need to switch places or pick up the slack. Choose up to four allies; you may change your chosen allies after spending a few hours training with them. You and those allies can each use Help as a bonus action, but only to aid you or one of your chosen allies. After you or an ally uses this feature, that person cannot use it again until they finish a short or long rest.

Additionally, as a bonus action you can shout a line from an inspiring song to grant an ally a Bardic Inspiration die, a d6. The die becomes a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level. This functions as the bard feature except that after you use this feature once, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

You are proficient with one type of musical instrument and with water vehicles.

Not content with a single robot assistant, you’ve managed to rig up a complex control system for an entire swarm of machines. You gain the following benefits:

  • Your Intelligence score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You can control up to 5 drones using the same control device and you can issue commands to any or all of them using the same bonus action.
You can wield pistols in both hands at the same time.  Simple, one-handed light firearms gain the dual-wielding property while you use them.

Your skill and deftness with code is amazing, and you gain the following benefits:

  • When you initiate a contested hack you may attempt to also make an Intelligence check to forge digital credentials at the same DC. If both succeed the hack is treated as uncontested so long as you only use the following hacking maneuvers: Bug Line, Copy Database, Delete Data, Digital Vanishing, Implant Data, Rig the Results, and Search Files.
  • You gain an expertise die on computers tool checks.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Secret Agent feat

Your long and varied career has taught you much in the way of spycraft. You gain the following benefit:

  • Choose three of the following feats: Empathic, Intuitive, Keen Intellect, Linguistics Expert, Thespian, or Weapons Specialist. You gain all of the features associated with your chosen feats that do not increase your ability scores.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Targeting Scrutiny feat

Your custom mech has a fusion core that can be used as a powerful explosive in emergencies. As an action you can safely doff your custom mecha armor and eject yourself 60 feet away from it. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. At the end of your turn, the custom mecha armor explodes in a 30 foot radius of power. Each creature in the area makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Science save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes 8d10 force damage + your Favored Ordnance damage die, or half damage on a success.

Your philosophy can affect reality. You are proficient in Culture and Dwarvish.

Additionally, choose one of the following philosophies and gain its associated feature.

You can also use a bonus action to grant that same feature to a creature you touch, which it must use in the next hour. After you grant the feature in this way, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest. Granting the feature doesn’t prevent you from using it yourself.

Eschatology. You are prepared to avoid bad endings. Once per hour when your hit points fall to 0, you may immediately stabilize. For the next round thereafter you cannot die, and damage you take doesn’t cause you to start dying.

If you touch a creature to share your feature and that creature died in the past round, it is returned to life at 0 hit points, stable, and is treated as if it had failed no death saving throws. For the next round thereafter it cannot die, and damage it takes doesn’t cause it to start dying.

Muktism. You can achieve brief transcendent freedom. Once per hour on your turn you may gain the benefits of the @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.adbxdvi3uj851e70]{freedom of movement}  spell until the end of your next turn. During this time you have the Incorporeal Movement trait (you can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. If you end your turn inside an object, you take 1d10 force damage and are shunted to the nearest empty space.)

Solipsistic Nihilism. You have clarity and control over your mind. Once per hour you can gain the benefits of the @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.wad0cgw4tcdbuvbr]{mind blank} spell until the end of your next turn. During this time you can also ignore any effects that compel your actions or control your emotions.

You have a knack for blending into a crowd.

  • If you enter or start your turn in a crowd of creatures with which you share a creature type, you are considered unseen to creatures that are not part of the crowd and gain advantage on Stealth checks to hide in the crowd. You must stay within the crowd to retain this benefit, and it may end early if you take any actions that would seem out of line with the crowd (such as bursting into song, casting a showy spell, or not participating in the crowd’s ritualistic chanting), as determined by the Narrator. If the crowd is targeted by an effect that requires a saving throw , you may choose to fail it to remain hidden.
  • You gain an expertise die to Sleight of Hand checks.

Whether you’re a former member of the constabulary or you’ve just had your share of run-ins with the city guards, you’ve developed a familiarity with how law enforcement tends to work.

  • Three times per long rest , you can use your reaction to gain advantage on skill checks opposed by members of local law enforcement.
  • You can use the @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-maneuvers.Item.9umrahwm68f81d7l]{Grapple} simple maneuver to attempt to restrain an unwilling creature with manacles, even if it is not restrained or both prone and grappled, as long as you are holding the manacles and have one free hand.
  • You have advantage on rolls to escape from, break, or pick the locks of manacles.

Hours of training have given you exceptionally fast hands, granting you the following benefits:

  • You may reload or load a light firearm or caster once per turn without using an action.
  • You may reload or load a medium or heavy firearm or caster as a bonus action
  • You gain expertise on Sleight of Hand checks involving weapons, cards, or bullets.

Prerequisite: Power Caster , proficiency in Arcana

The practitioners of the darkest arcane arts in Elissar work spells that press upon the boundaries of the realms material, and those within the Festung are the only users of magic that dare to defy the very nature of the world. The fell individuals that practice their crafts within the shadowy halls of the isolated keep do not dissuade new students, but only those with darkness in their hearts are willing to stay and witness what happens within long enough to learn the dangerous secrets of its corrupt mages.

Your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score increases by 1, and your maximum for that ability score increases by 1.

You treat the rare conjuration spells of Elissar as normal spells (see Rare Conjurations in Elissar), and add all spells of the summoning school to your class spell list. You are able to learn these spells when gaining a level in a spellcasting class or from other mages in the Festung.

You learn the @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.o024bxc2jndzid88]{void maw} cantrip.

In addition, when you use rapid summoning to conjure a creature you can do so with only 2 rounds of casting (instead of 1d4+1 rounds).

Prerequisite: Festung Apprentice

Within the bowels of the Festung are grimoires and tomes only the most dedicated mages are allowed to access, the teachings inside of such import and danger that even their existence is a well-kept secret that just a handful of people in Elissar know about. Only those with true darkness in their hearts are given leave to read from this forbidden library, its safety insured by their wicked compact.

You gain the Evil trait and radiate an Evil aura.

Your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score increases by 1, and your maximum for that ability score increases by 1.

In addition, you learn how to bind a summoned creature to you. To bind a summoned creature you must cast its conjuration spell in a 1 hour ritual that costs 100 gold in components, expending a spell slot one level higher. You do not have to concentrate on the spell and the summoned creature remains bound to you until it dies or you spend an action to dismiss it. While you have bound a summoned creature, you cannot regain the spell slot expended to conjure it and you are unable to cast spells of the summoning school.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Iceborn

With little more than a thought you can project an arctic chill in front of you to propel yourself through the world. You can use a bonus action to spend 2 sorcery points and freeze the ground just ahead of you as you move, creating a pathway of ice that increases your movement speed by a number of feet equal to 10 × your proficiency bonus until the end of your turn. Your ice pathway remains until the end of your next turn. Other creatures treat the ice pathway as difficult terrain , and when it moves across your ice pathway or ends its turn there it must make a Dexterity saving throw against your maneuver DC or fall prone .

You can create an ice pathway to tread on air or across other surfaces that could not support your weight as long as you end your turn on a square that can support your weight or above an unoccupied square no further beneath you than a number of feet equal to 10 × your proficiency bonus, in which case you can use an action to create a temporary ice pylon to support your ice pathway. Otherwise, you fall as normal. An ice pylon has an AC equal to your maneuver DC, hit points equal to your level, and disappears with the ice pathway.You cannot ascend at a greater angle than 45 degrees, moving half your Speed while doing so.

In addition, when using Ice Armor you can spend 2 additional sorcery points at the start of your next turn to increase its duration by 1 round.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Strategic Thinker feat

You know how to obscure your intentions while setting in place subtle strategies to confound your foes. You gain the following benefits:

  • You gain an expertise die with board games.
  • Other creatures have disadvantage on Insight checks against you.
  • The range of your Commanding Presence increases by 10 feet.
  • When you take the Ready action, a friendly creature within range of your Commanding Presence that can see and hear you can immediately make a single attack as though you had chosen to forgo one of your own attacks. You cannot designate your ally’s attack or any of its direct,  immediate consequences as the trigger for your Ready action.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Amped Up Feat

You can use technology to push the power of your spells far beyond their normal limits. You gain the following benefit:

  • Once per long rest, you may choose a spell you have prepared as a spell invention that requires a saving throw and change its range to a 60-foot cone or a 20-foot radius sphere centered on yourself (but excluding the square of origin), affecting all valid targets within range. Doing so causes the spell invention to immediately fizzle upon casting, regardless of the results of the fizzle die.

You gain proficiency in Nature.

Your trips and tribulations bond you with the environment. When you are prone , attacks against you don’t have advantage . (A character can intentionally fall prone on their turn without spending any actions or movement, but cannot intentionally fall prone when it is not their turn.)

Additionally, when you become prone you can gain a link to the normally quiescent spirits of nature. When you stand up, choose yourself or a creature you are aware of. That creature gains resistance to all damage and advantage on all saving throws until the start of your next turn.

This might take the form of a tree branch blocking an attack, stones shifting under an ally’s feet to nudge him to safety, a tendril of water harrying an enemy, or even a gust of wind screaming a distraction. The link then ends. A given creature cannot benefit from this protection more than once per encounter.

When you fail a death saving throw in a natural area, you can gain the benefits of @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.pdwrag8eq7r0ldcp]{commune with nature} when you regain consciousness. After you use this ability you cannot use it again until you complete a long rest.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Game Theorist Feat

You know how to choose the perfect moment to launch all of your carefully constructed plans into action. You gain the following benefits:

  • You gain an expertise die with board games and your expertise die maximum for board games increases to 1d10, exceeding the usual limit on expertise die.
  • Once per short rest, you can use an action to select a number of creatures equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1) within range of your Commanding Presence and move their turn in initiative to come immediately after yours in an order you designate for the remainder of the combat. This order can still change if a creature delays its turn, is rendered unconscious, or otherwise leaves the initiative order. You may not use this ability during a surprise round or on your first turn in combat.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Divine Spark feat

You can harness a sliver of the divine power that brought creation into being. You gain the following benefits:

  • You learn the @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.pblaa5w3f6tuqxuj]{mending} and @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.omvngnmoo75is54f]{spare the dying} cantrips and they do not count toward your spells known. You may cast both cantrips using a single action if the both are directed toward a single, valid target. If you already know one of these cantrips, you instead learn another cantrip from the artificer or cleric spell list.
  • You may spend a use of channel divinity as an action to touch a living creature and replace any body parts the creature is missing (except for any necessary for life, such as the head or heart) with prosthetics that the creature can operate at will (see Equipment in Chapter 4: Adventurer’s Guide). If a creature regains a body part this way, you may also choose to expend 500 gold as part of the action to grant it a single augment from a constructed heritage gift (from Gate Pass Gazette #0) for so long as the creature uses the prosthetic body part. A creature may not benefit from more than one augment in this way, and such augments only function for the creature they were created for. At the Narrator’s discretion, certain augments may only be available when replacing certain body parts.
  • When you gain this feat, you may choose to replace one of your own body parts with an augmented prosthetic at no cost. You only gain this benefit once.

You gain proficiency in Intimidation and Elvish.

Once per month you can cast @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.kbyg7uvh3w8osgiq]{sending} without components, but only to contact Vekeshi mystics you are aware of.

In battle, a vestige of the power of Srasama waits to punish those who harm you or your allies. When an enemy you’re aware of deals damage to you or one of your allies, you can use your reaction to deal 2d10 radiant damage to it. That enemy sees a faint burning outline of a six-armed goddess hovering behind you, armed with blades of fire. After you use this feature you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

At 5th level, the damage increases to 3d10. At 11th level, the enemy also catches on fire, taking 1d10 ongoing fire damage until an action is used to douse the flames. At 17th level, the ongoing fire damage increases to 2d10.

activation.reactionTrigger: When an enemy you’re aware of deals damage to you or one of your allies

system.description:
Prerequisite: Proficiency with Stealth

You become particularly adept at altering weapons to better hide them on your person and at sneaking them past most guards. This alteration may consist of flattening out a blade, adding elaborate decoration to a weapon to disguise its utility, concealing a weapon inside another object, or similar tactics.

You gain the ability to rework certain existing weapons to have the Stealthy quality, provided you have the appropriate tools. This alteration takes half as long as crafting a new weapon of its kind but requires the same DC (see Between Adventures in Chapter 7: Adventuring, Adventurer’s Guide). You gain advantage on such crafting checks and gain a 1d6 expertise die on checks to craft a new item with the Stealthy quality.

Altering existing weapons to give them the Stealthy quality costs 25 gp or half the item’s cost, whichever is higher. You can alter the following: brass knuckles, daggers, dueling daggers, punching daggers, throwing daggers, whips, short swords, slings, darts, hand crossbows and garottes. Work with the Narrator to decide what form this alteration takes.

As a rule, weapons can have no more than three properties unless one of those properties is a restriction.

Finally, you gain an expertise die on checks to hide a weapon on your person and on Sleight of Hand checks to discreetly draw or use such a weapon.

Prerequisite: Charisma 13 or higher

Journeying through the unforgiving Hinterlands has made you a hardy traveler, as well as an expert on dealing with the orcs that call it home. Whether you are merely a tolerated observer or have become familiar with orcs among the tribes there, you have learned a great deal from your time with them.

  • Your Wisdom or Charisma increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You learn Orcish.
  • You gain an expertise die on Culture, Insight, History, and Religion checks related to orcs.

In addition, you gain the following feature.

Full-Hearted Holler. The orcs of the Hinterlands have revealed some of their secret understandings about emotions and impulses, and taught you some mastery of the art of pathos. You can use a bonus action to make a passionate outburst that motivates your allies. Each friendly creature within 30 feet of you gains an expertise die that it can use on an ability check or saving throw it makes within the next 10 minutes. After you have used this feature, it cannot be used again until you finish a long rest.

Whether it’s rebuilding vehicles from scrap or upgrading new ones, you’re as good with a wrench as you are behind the wheel. You gain the following benefits:

  • Your Intelligence or Constitution score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • If you have access to a personal vehicle or starfighter, during a short rest you can apply one of the following: increase its weight capacity by 50%; double its supply capacity; or increase the collision damage it deals (but does not take) by 50%. A vehicle can only benefit from one effect at a time.
  • If you have access to a personal vehicle or starfighter, during a long rest you can choose two of the short rest improvements or add +1d6 damage to one weapons system connected to the vehicle.

All modifications work only for you, though if a vehicle is loaded with doubled Supply and another creature pilots it, the supplies remain packed but their checks to pilot the vehicle are made at disadvantage due to the unwieldiness of the craft.

Prerequisite: Ace Starfighter combat tradition

Your daring and mastery of starfighter combat make you a legend. You gain the following benefits:

  • Your Charisma score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • When piloting a starfighter in combat you gain 2 temporary exertion when you roll initiative. These exertion points can only be used for Ace Starfighter combat maneuvers and last until used or the combat ends.
  • Your maneuver save DC for starfighter maneuvers increases by +1.

Prerequisite: Proficiency with land vehicles

You have become an expert dog sledder—perhaps taught by one of the Steam Striders of Skappa—and are superb at both caring for your hardworking dogs and your vehicle. You gain the following benefits.

  • You gain advantage on Animal Handling checks made against dogs and draft animals.
  • You gain an expertise die on checks made to use, maintain, repair, or modify a dog sled.
  • You have figured out ways of improving dog sleds by making them sturdier, adding room for an extra passenger.
  • Allies able to see you driving a dog sled gain proficiency with dog sleds while they are able to see you.

In addition, you gain the following feature.

Incredible Mush. You can inspire incredible energy in sled dogs by spending 1 minute loudly and enthusiastically encouraging them. Until the end of its next long rest, each sled dog able to hear and see your encouragement gains advantage on saving throws against fatigue and increases its Speed by 15 feet. Once you have used this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: 3 levels in berserker, 3 levels in fighter

Rage sets a berserker apart from other warriors and makes them monoliths of combat able to withstand incredible punishment—but it can also be a source of tremendous might. You have discovered how to tap into your fury to magnify your prowess and prove you are the strongest of all.

While you are raging, you can spend exertion in the following ways:

  • When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can spend up to a number of exertion points equal to your proficiency bonus, dealing 1d4 extra damage for each exertion point spent.
  • When you make a Strength ability check, you can spend exertion (up to a maximum equal to your proficiency bonus) to gain a 1d4 bonus to the check for every 2 exertion points spent.
  • When you attempt to @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-maneuvers.Item.9umrahwm68f81d7l]{grapple} a creature or when a creature you are grappling attempts to break the grapple, you can spend exertion (up to a maximum equal to your fighter level) to increase your maneuver DC by 1d4 for every 3 exertion points spent.
system.prerequisite: 3 levels in berserker, 3 levels in fighter

system.description:
Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: 3 levels in adept, 3 levels in sorcerer, Manifestation (Blizzard)

In the depths of your heart there is a chill you have learned how to truly harness, turning your deep connection to the cold to manifest it around yourself. You gain the Ice Armor feature.

@UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.5ulns0a481fxakkm]{Ice Armor.} When you deal cold damage with a spell of 1st-level or higher, you can spend 2 sorcery points to briefly encase yourself in form-fitting magical ice that protects you from harm without hindering you in any way. While encased in this magical ice you gain immunity to cold damage, resistance to fire damage, and resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons. The magical ice evaporates when you take damage equal to or greater than your level, or at the start of your next turn.
system.prerequisite: 3 levels in adept, 3 levels in sorcerer, Manifestation (Blizzard)

system.description:
Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Haleg Scepen feat

You know the secret to creating life from inanimate material. You gain the following benefit:

  • You learn the @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.6l4bmc7ovgcn2c9k]{find familiar} spell, but the material component is replaced with 10 gold worth alchemical reagents, consumed by the spell. This does not count toward your spells known. Any creature you summon using this feature is considered a construct instead of its usual creature type. You may also summon a homunculus when casting the spell in this way.
  • You may cast animate objects once per long rest as though using a 5th-level spell slot. If you concentrate on the spell for its full duration, you may also choose to impart sentience to one of the animated objects.In addition to the stats it gains as an animated object, the object gains Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores of 10, senses identical to those of a human, and learns one language you know. If the object does not have any structure that would correspond to a mouth, it can speak telepathically to any creature within 30 feet of it with which it shares a language. Objects awakened in this manner are charmed by you for 30 days or until your or your companions harm them. During this period, you may revoke the sentience of such objects by touching them and spending an action. Objects that lose their sentience cannot be targeted by spells and effects that normally target dead creatures such as @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.0k5zymq9q95l8jwa]{revivify} or @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.6ia3gup3j0m6oigb]{speak with dead}. Afterward, the object may choose to remain friendly to you depending on how it was treated while charmed.

Notes for Imago Dei

With the permission of the Narrator, you may instead choose to roll 4d4 three times and use the results for the object’s Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores when using the Imago Dei feat.

If revoking sentience is morally unsettling for you or your character, consider flavoring this feat as having the ability to bind and unbind spirits to objects such that the spirits persist in an immaterial form between bindings.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Tremendously Hulking

There are countless legends speaking of warriors as mighty as you, their weaponry cast away in their fury and replaced by trees or boulders.

When you enter a rage, you can spend 8 exertion points to increase your size category by two steps (from Small to Large or from Medium to Huge) for the duration of your rage. While your size is increased, your Speed increases by 15 feet, your weapon attacks deal an extra 2d4 damage, your maneuver DC increases by 4, and your reach increases by 5 feet.

In addition, you gain proficiency with improvised weapons. Improvised weapons that you throw have a range of 50/150 feet. While you are raging, one-handed improvised weapons you wield deal 1d8 for Small, 1d10 for Medium, or 1d12 for Large; two-handed improvised weapons you wield deal 2d4 for Small, 2d6 for Medium, or 2d8 for Large; and your range for thrown improvised weapons doubles.

Where other people see useless scraps, you see integral parts to ingenious devices. You gain the following benefits.

  • You gain an expertise die on all Engineering checks.
  • You can take random assortments of items and transform them into something useful. With 10 minutes work and access to refuse, junk, or natural forest litter you can create any item worth 10 gold or less from the Tool Kit, Survival Gear, or Miscellaneous Adventuring Gear item lists. Items you create in this way are functional, but have no gold value and can’t be used by creatures other than yourself. You can create a number of items equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all uses whenever you finish a long rest.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Thought Feaster feat

Like a sculptor at the clay you reshape the thoughts of others or perhaps more like the patient zero of some cognitive virus your underhanded thoughts spread to those around you.

As a bonus action you can form or end a psychic connection with a willing creature you can see or hear. Creatures you form this connection with gain the benefits of any clever tricks you know as if they had those class features. Any clever tricks they perform use your clever tricks save DC, and if they would require spending a Dastardly Gambit die they may expend one of yours if you permit it. In addition, while you have this connection formed you and the creature can communicate telepathically, even if you do not share a language. You can connect with up to a number of creatures in this way equal to your Charisma modifier.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: 3 levels in artificer , 3 levels in rogue

You have all the tools needed for clandestine missions. You gain the following benefits:

  • Your Dexterity or Intelligence score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You can use Tactical Chemistry and a Cunning Action using the same bonus action.
  • You gain the schematic for a magic weapon of up to rare rarity of your choice that has either the ranged or the finesse property.
  • You gain the Boobytrapper, Delay Trap, or Locksmith skill trick, or another skill trick if you already know all three, and it does not count against the number of skill tricks you know.
system.prerequisite: 3 levels in artificer , 3 levels in rogue

system.description:
Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: 3 levels in artificer , 3 levels in savant

Your mind is equipped to crack any problem. You gain the following benefits:

  • Your Dexterity or Intelligence score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You can prepare a savant trick and use Tactical Chemistry using the same bonus action.
  • You gain the Timely Tool trick (or another trick if you already know it) and it does not count against the number of tricks you know.
  • When you use Analyze Need, you may choose a tool proficiency instead of a skill proficiency.
system.prerequisite: 3 levels in artificer , 3 levels in savant

system.description:
Prerequisite: Ace Starfighter combat tradition

Unable to really focus on a single activity and favoring a split focus, you may choose two Journey Activities for a given region, but gain 1 level of fatigue if both activities are physical, or 1 strife if one or both activities are largely mental. If you critically succeed at one task, you cannot critically succeed at the other and only succeed instead.

In addition, an ability score of your choice increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.

If you take the Repair journey activity on a starship you can instead augment its abilities in one of the following ways:

  • The ship’s shield modulator is improved, granting 10% more temporary hit points until the next time the shields have been broken. On a critical success, the increase is 20%.
  • The ship’s engines are improved, increasing impulse speed by one step or FTL speed by one point. This benefit lasts one week, or one month on a critical success.
  • The ship’s computer system is improved, granting anyone on the ship expertise on their next Journey Activity, or advantage on a critical success.

In addition your Intelligence score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20

Quelling any trace of seasickness, rubbing elbows with pirates and sailors alike, and fully acclimating to the seafaring lifestyle has gained you the following benefits.

● Your Dexterity or Charisma increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.

● You learn Thieves’ Cant. If you already know Thieves’ Cant, instead you gain an expertise die when using it to make a Deception, Intimidation, or Persuasion check.

● You also learn the other universal language of pirates: fistfighting. You can roll 1d4 in place of your normal damage for unarmed strikes.

● With your newfound sealegs, you gain an expertise die on Acrobatics and Athletics checks made on a boat.

● You can always tell the strength and direction of the wind, you gain a 1d6 expertise die on navigator’s tools checks, and so long as you are able to see the stars you can  use them to make navigator’s tools checks.

You recognize the use of strange artifacts immediately and can intuitively grasp how they function. You gain the following benefits:

  • Your Intelligence score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You learn the @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.dgms08g84zdlbr81]{identify} spell and can cast it without components or expending a spell slot once per long rest.
  • You can attune to a magic item after spending 10 minutes in contact with it, rather than over a short rest as normal.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Void Lightning feat

Reality and morality are flimsy barriers for the weak minded that you have long since broken through and left behind. You gain the following benefits:

  • Whenever you make a Deception check, you may add one of your Dastardly Gambit dice without expending a die.
  • Manipulation comes as easy as breathing to you. You can manifest the psionic power push thought without expending any psionic points. After manifesting the power in this way, creature targeted by it gains advantage on saving throws made to resist it for the next 24 hours.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Starsword Whisperer feat

You empathically feel for machines—you’ve felt their minds and tend to think of them as innocent, enslaved creatures that simply don’t understand the concept of freedom. Concepts can be taught, however.

Whenever you finish an uncontested hack or are locked out of a contested hack, you can choose to liberate the device. Devices that are liberated in this way treat all potential users as hostile threats regardless of credentials or passwords for the duration of their high alert. Other creatures attempting to use a liberated device in this way while it is on high alert must successfully hack back into it, ending the device’s liberation on a success.

Your psionic powers bolster your physical abilities and augment your combat prowess. You gain the following benefits:

  • You learn the adrenalize and imbue weapon reflexes.
  • You gain a psionic point pool of 1 or increase your existing pool of psionic points by 1.

Research is important for science and for combat. If you don’t know just the right fighting technique, you’re pretty sure someone else has published a thesis about it.

You gain proficiency in one martial melee and one martial ranged weapon.

Additionally, you can make limited use of tricks from the savant class (page 45). You learn two savant tricks—typically Committed Defense Aegis and Experimental Flourish—and can acquire other techniques in your travels.

You can use a bonus action to prepare a trick you know (like a savant). Once you have done so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

If you are a savant with this feat, simply add the two tricks you picked to the list of tricks you know. You can prepare them as you would any other tricks.

You can also learn additional tricks by finding a copy of the thesis they wrote. If you have a copy of a thesis, when you complete a long rest you can replace one of the tricks you know with the trick detailed in the thesis. See Martial Scientist Theses (page 210) for a list of prominent theses and their associated tricks.

Prerequisite: The ability to cast at least one spell of 1st-level or higher

You have specialized in conjuring creatures from beyond to fight on your behalf. You gain the following benefits:

  • You learn the direct minion cantrip. It does not count against your number of cantrips known.
  • Select one spell which conjures creatures, has a casting time of 1 minute, and is of a level you can cast. If you prepare spells, you always have the spell prepared. If you learn spells, add it to your list of known spells. It does not count toward your number of known spells. Whenever you gain a level, you can replace the spell with another that fulfills the requirements.
  • When you use rapid summoning to conjure a creature, the number of rounds you need to spend casting is halved, rounded up.
system.prerequisite: The ability to cast at least one spell of 1st-level or higher

system.description:
Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: 3 levels in scientist, 3 levels in trooper

With both combat and technical training, mecha aces turn their brains into brawn by designing and controlling their own unique custom mecha. So long as you have access to your gear, you can construct your own custom mecha over the course of a long rest. This custom mecha acts as a special set of armor for you and has the following properties:

  • While wearing your custom mecha, your AC is equal to 12 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier.
  • Your custom mecha has the hackable and spacefaring properties, and it includes 6 mod ports.
  • If damaged or broken your custom mecha can be repaired with a DC 15 multitool check.
  • Your size increases by 1 category (from Small to Medium or from Medium to Large) while wearing your custom mecha.
  • While wearing your custom mecha you have disadvantage on Stealth checks and advantage on Strength checks.
  • Your custom mecha is encoded to you and it is inoperable for any other creature.
  • Your custom mecha has 2 special weapon ports with the advanced weapon hatch mods in addition to its 6 mod ports. These special weapon port mods cannot be changed. Weapons mounted on these special ports only ever require a single wielding hand to fire, even if they have the two-handed property.
  • Whenever you make an attack using a weapon attached to one of your special weapon ports, you can use a bonus action to attack with the weapon mounted on the other special weapon port.
  • Any weapons mounted on your custom mecha are considered favored ordnance weapons for you.
  • The cost to install armor mods on your custom mecha is reduced by half.

If your custom mecha is ever lost or destroyed, you can create another one using 250 credits worth of materials over the course of a long rest.

In addition, you gain an expertise die on saving throws while piloting a mecha starfighter and while crewing the deck of a mecha capital ship.
system.prerequisite: 3 levels in scientist, 3 levels in trooper

system.description:
Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: Talented Telepath

With experience your telepathic powers grow stronger, creating a bond not just between minds but between souls as well. Once between rounds, you can choose to expend a spell slot to grant exertion points to a creature that is part of your Telepathic Link. The creature gains 2 exertion points for a 1st-level spell slot, and 2 more for each spell slot level above 1st. Alternatively, you can instead spend exertion points to restore a spell slot to a creature within your Telepathic Link. The creature gains a 1st-level spell slot for 3 exertion points, a 2nd-level spell slot for 6 exertion points, a 3rd-level spell slot for 9 exertion points, or a 4th-level spell slot for 12 exertion points. The creature must be able to cast spells of that level to benefit from this feature.

Additionally, your Telepathic Link feature now has no range limit as long as those benefiting from it are on the same plane.

Through training and dedication you’ve become an invaluable member of any crew, and gain the following benefits:

  • Your Intelligence or Charisma score increase by 1, to a maximum of 20.
  • You count as 3 people for the purpose of a minimum crew for a capital ship.
  • When you use a capital ship’s weapons to attack a starfighter you gain advantage on the attack roll.
  • During boarding mass combat you increase your faction’s total by an additional 2d6.

Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: 3 levels in psion, 3 levels in scout

When a powerful personality is blessed with psionic gifts their coercive words can become nearly impossible to resist. Thoughts and feelings can intermingle and shift so subtly that the mind can truly be reshaped at will. You gain the following benefits:

  • Your power rating is treated as if it were 1 higher for the purpose of learning and manifesting psionic powers from the telepathic discipline.
  • As a bonus action, you can recover a number of Dastardly Gambit dice up to your maximum at the cost of 1 psionic point per Dastardly Gambit die recovered in this way.
  • You can psionically reshape your tactics when you feel thoughts wander down unfavorable paths. Whenever you roll a Charisma check or saving throw, you can spend a psionic point to reroll it. You must decide to make this reroll after the die is rolled but before the Narrator tells you the results.
system.prerequisite: 3 levels in psion, 3 levels in scout

system.description:
Synergy Feat. Prerequisite: 3 levels in druid , 3 levels in savant
